svg.aria-label: Diagram of SCP coverage across an organisation. At the top, the management account sits outside the guardrail: service control policies do not affect users or roles in it, which is deliberate because the account that writes the guardrails cannot be locked out by them. Below, a shaded region shows SCP coverage over every member account including each account's root user, and including a security tooling account registered as a delegated administrator, which remains a member account and stays governed. At the bottom, the four categories an SCP cannot restrict: any action by the management account, anything using service-linked role permissions, a short list of root-user tasks, and a few AWS-related services.
svg.title: Which accounts service control policies actually govern, and why the management account is exempt by design
svg.text: One account in the organisation is not governed by the organisation
Every design decision about the management account follows from a single documented exemption.
Management account — outside the guardrail
SCPs don't affect users or roles here.
Anything you run in it is ungoverned by definition.
Why it is exempt, and why that is correct
The account that authors the guardrails cannot be subject to them,
or one bad policy would lock the organisation out of its own repair.
Inside the guardrail
SCP coverage — every member account, including each account's own root user
Workload account
Governed. An administrator
here cannot exceed the SCP,
even with AdministratorAccess.
Security tooling account
Registered as delegated
administrator — and still a
member account. SCPs apply.
Log archive account
Governed. This is the
property that makes a
retention guarantee real.
What an SCP cannot restrict, whatever you write in it
• Any action performed by the management account
• Any action performed using permissions attached to a service-linked role
• A short list of root-user tasks — Enterprise support registration, CloudFront trusted signer, reverse DNS configuration
• Tasks on a few AWS-related services outside the main API surface
Delegating administration does not move work outside the guardrail. It moves work inside one, which is the entire argument for doing it.
